analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 11.12.26
key_insights: Futures are lower (Nasdaq -95bps, S&P -40bps, Russell -15bps). NVDA is down about 7.5% premarket after a WSJ report that its board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang. The board could meet as soon as today.
The AI complex is trading lower on the NVDA news: SMH -2.5%, DRAM -3.5%, neoclouds -5% to -10%. AVGO and AMD are up about 2% each on share-gain optimism.

The reported reasons for the possible ouster are two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. NYT reports a relationship with an Nvidia executive who reports to Huang. Bloomberg says Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify CEO candidates. Semafor says some directors favor CFO Kress as interim CEO.

BABA is down 4% premarket on concerns that cloud operators' access to advanced Nvidia chips may face tighter US scrutiny. Alibaba rents Nvidia chips through Singapore-based Megaspeed International, whose founder had an affair with Huang and is suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.
Bloomberg says the Nvidia fallout puts the US-China trade truce to the test as Xi welcomes Trump.

GS Econ expects AI-related hardware and intellectual property spending to exceed $900bn annualized by end-2026 (up $550bn from 2025) and reach $1.4tn by end-2027 (up a further $500bn), roughly 4% of US GDP.

GS Econ says official statistics will understate the AI capex boost. Semiconductor investment is undercounted, and most information processing equipment is imported and netted out of GDP. AI adds 5.3pp to true 2027 capex growth but 4.3pp to measured capex growth, and 0.6pp to true GDP growth but 0.2pp to measured GDP growth.
GS Econ forecasts 2027 real business fixed investment growth of 8% Q4/Q4, versus consensus of 4.2%. It forecasts 2027 real GDP growth of 2.4% Q4/Q4.
The US 10-year yield is a touch higher at 5% and crude is down 70bps. Several Fed speakers today, who collectively have been quite hawkish this week.

Asia closed lower (Shanghai -67bps, Hang Seng -1.26%, Nikkei -70bps, Kospi -61bps) with no regional catalyst. Europe is higher (FTSE +35bps, DAX +65bps, CAC +70bps) on light volumes, 25% below the 10-day average.
Earnings today: NBIS and LGN before the open. AMAT, CBRS, CSCO, DLO, GEMI, LFTO, NMAX, NU and STNE after the close. PPI is due Friday 11/13.
Most active high-touch names: INTC, MSFT, NVDA, UBER, RBLX, AMZN, GOOGL, AVGO, TTD, MTCH.
